result.summary: Turns the `building-on` triplet evaluation in `contrib/guix/toolchains.scm` from a top-level variable evaluated at module load time into a procedure. This ensures derivations evaluate their `--build` triplet dynamically under the system specified by `--system` rather than locking in the host system.
result.problem: When running Guix under foreign architectures (for example, building for `aarch64-linux` on an `x86_64` host using emulation), `guix shell` loads manifests before applying `--system`. `building-on` therefore captures the host architecture, configuring cross-toolchain packages like `gcc-cross-sans-libc` with mismatched `--build` triplets and causing configure-time failures.
evidence: PR description: `gcc-cross-sans-libc` fails to configure with `checking for CET support... configure: error: compiler and assembler with CET support are required for --enable-cet` when running `--system=aarch64-linux` on an x86_64 host
PR description: author verified that native builds produce identical derivations on master and with this PR, leaving standard release builds unchanged
result.scope_notes: Small 4-line Guile Scheme adjustment in Guix toolchain manifests.
result.card: Turns the Guix `building-on` triplet resolution in `contrib/guix/toolchains.scm` into a procedure evaluated per derivation rather than at module load time. When running Guix with `--system` on a host of a different architecture (such as via emulation), Guix manifests previously locked in the host system triplet, causing cross-compiler packages like `gcc-cross-sans-libc` to fail configuration. The change enables cross-architecture Guix container builds while leaving derivations for native release builds identical.

risk.why: Mistakes in Guix toolchain derivations could alter or break reproducible release builds across supported environments.
